proposal: The Mandate recommends that funding to postsecondary institutions be block-granted and narrowed to Historically Black Colleges and Universities and tribally controlled colleges, as part of working with Congress to eliminate or move Office of Postsecondary Education programs (p. 327). status_summary: The Department of Education announced in September 2025 (page last reviewed 2025-09-10) that it would end discretionary funding for seven Title III and Title V minority-serving institution grant programs and reprogram about $350 million of FY2025 funds, while about $132 million in mandatory funds could not be redirected. Its FY2027 congressional justification shows that about $438 million was reprogrammed to Strengthening HBCUs and about $57 million to Strengthening Tribally Controlled Colleges in FY2025, consistent with a 2025-09-15 news report of about $495 million in one-time funding for those institutions. The FY2027 request keeps the HBCU and tribal college discretionary lines at their FY2026 levels (about $406 million and $54 million), proposes zero for Strengthening Institutions and the Hispanic-serving institution programs, proposes no block grant or consolidation of institutional aid, holds Gallaudet, the National Technical Institute for the Deaf and the American Printing House for the Blind flat, and cuts Howard University by $50 million. Because the text asks for legislation, these executive steps and budget proposals are staged as proposed.

timeline.event: The Department of Education announced it was ending discretionary funding for seven Title III and Title V minority-serving institution grant programs and reprogramming about $350 million of FY2025 funds; about $132 million in mandatory Title III Part F and HSI STEM funds was not redirected (month-only date).

The Department of Education announced about $495 million in additional one-time FY2025 funding for HBCUs and tribally controlled colleges, after ending the minority-serving institution discretionary grants.
The Department announced a postsecondary education partnership under which the Department of Labor takes a greater role in administering most Higher Education Act postsecondary grant programs.
The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75) was approved; Division B funds the Department of Education for FY2026.

The FY2027 President's budget request for the Department of Education (month-only date) keeps discretionary Strengthening HBCUs at about $406 million and Strengthening Tribally Controlled Colleges at about $54 million, their FY2026 levels and below FY2025 amounts that included reprogrammed funds, proposes zero for Strengthening Institutions and Hispanic-serving institution programs, holds Gallaudet, NTID and the American Printing House for the Blind flat, and cuts Howard University from about $304 million to about $254 million.

title: Block-grant institutional aid, narrow it to HBCUs and tribal colleges, phase out earmarks
uncertainties: The minority-serving institution press release prints no day; it was last reviewed on 2025-09-10 and is dated to September 2025 here, and it does not name the recipients of the reprogrammed funds. The FY2025 reprogramming amounts for HBCUs and tribal colleges come from the FY2027 justification; the 2025-09-15 announcement date rests on a news report, and no Department release for it was opened. The FY2027 budget documents print no date; April 2026 is used (a law-firm summary gives 2026-04-03). The FY2027 justification was read through about nine tenths of its length. The FY2026 request and its consolidation proposals could not be opened, and FY2026 enacted levels for individual institutional aid lines were not read in the law text; the FY2026 levels cited come from the FY2027 justification. The justification cites a 2025-12-02 Justice Department legal opinion on race-based eligibility, which was not read. No bill block-granting institutional aid was found; an HBCU infrastructure bill (H.R. 8791, introduced 2026-05-13) was noted in research but its text was not read.
